description: Agent Construction: submit a payment application or draw request with the contract, the schedule of values and the prior payment records: the application with its number, the last day of its period, currency, contract sum, each continuation line with its id, the schedule line it bills, description, scheduled value, earlier work, work this period, stored materials, completed to date and percent, and its total completed and stored, retainage percent and amount, total earned less retainage, earlier certificates and amount due; optionally the contract with its sum to date, retainage percent and currency; optionally the schedule of values with each line’s id, description and scheduled value; and optionally the prior payment records with each payment’s id, application number, amount and day paid. The signed report gives the application, the contract, the schedule and the prior payments, each line matched to its schedule line with its completed to date recomputed, the lines unscheduled, billed past their value or misprinting their percent, the schedule lines unbilled, and the retainage, total earned, earlier certificates and amount due recomputed, and counts them, and names a divergent application: a contract sum or scheduled value unlike the records, a line outside the schedule of values, a line whose completed to date is not its earlier work plus this period plus stored materials, a line billed past its scheduled value, and a total completed, retainage, total earned, earlier certificates or amount due that does not recompute; then a schedule line left off, a misprinted percent and a schedule of values unlike the contract sum, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No contract, schedule of values, prior payment records, retainage percent or amount due leaves the application unverified. Amounts compare to the cent and percents to the half point. A construction payment application is a draw document read against the contract’s schedule of values and prior draws: wever_invoice-check reads an invoice against the job or mandate it claims to belong to, and wever_invoice-payment-match compares one invoice with one payment record, while the payment check recomputes each line, the retainage and the amount due against the schedule of values and the earlier payments. Verdict build_payment_divergent, build_payment_partial, build_payment_unverified or build_payment_consistent. POST /api/build-payment-check. Reads the construction paperwork supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only, with no structural, engineering or safety judgment, building-code compliance determination, valuation of work performed or legal advice on contracts, liens or permits, and the paperwork stays in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Construction reads supplied construction paperwork for consistency between documents: a building permit, a contractor license record, a bid, a construction contract, a change order, a lien waiver, a completion certificate or punch list record, and a payment application. Beside it, wever_workorder-create and the other wever_workorder tools and wever_agent-work-order-exchange are the action layer that creates, funds, delivers and releases work orders, while this family moves nothing and executes nothing and only reads paperwork; wever_agent-escrow-lite holds and releases escrowed funds, and escrow stays there; and the Agent Real Estate checks such as wever_realty-title-check read property records by parcel and address, not a project’s construction paperwork. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-construction-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-construction/.
